# Mahāvaccha Sutta (MN 73 (PTS MN i 489))

**ID:** MN 73 (PTS MN i 489)
**Section:** Majjhimanikāya (mn)
**Collection:** Sutta
**Title (Pali):** Mahāvaccha Sutta
**Title (English, from literature):** The Longer Discourse With Vacchagotta
**PTS:** MN i 489
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0202m.mul2.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mahāvaccha Sutta* (MN 73, PTS MN i 489; also known as the *Mahāvacchagotta Sutta*) is the seventy-third discourse of the *Majjhimanikāya* and forms the final installment in the collection's "Vacchagotta trilogy" [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination]. In this sutta, the wanderer Vacchagotta relinquishes speculative metaphysical questions to inquire directly into spiritual practice and realization. Vacchagotta asks whether the Buddha alone has achieved awakening or whether his disciples have done so as well [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination]. The Buddha answers that far more than five hundred disciples have reached each spiritual level: ordained monks and nuns have achieved arahantship, celibate laymen and laywomen have attained non-returning (*anāgāmitā*), and non-celibate householders enjoying sensual pleasures have attained once-returning (*sakadāgāmitā*) [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination; Goodwin 2012; Radich 2007; Wen, Study of Sukkhavipassaka; Collett 2014]. Convinced by this complete spiritual community, Vacchagotta receives ordination as a monk under the Buddha [Bodhi 1970]. Following the Buddha's instruction to cultivate serenity (*samatha*) and insight (*vipassanā*) in close cooperation, he develops the higher spiritual knowledges (*abhiññā* / *vijjā*) and attains arahantship [Bodhi 1970; Saitanaporn 2009; Shonin et al. 2015]. Buddhaghosa's commentary on the sutta also analyzes the synthesis of *samatha* and *vipassanā* in relation to the *abhiññās* [Saitanaporn 2009].

**Sources**

- [Bodhi 1970] Bhikkhu Bodhi, Numerical Discourses of the Buddha (1970) — Note on Vacchagotta's ordination and attainment of arahantship in MN 73
- [Bodhi, Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination] Bhikkhu Bodhi, The Revival of Bhikkhunī Ordination in the Theravāda Tradition — Account of Vacchagotta questioning the Buddha about the attainments of the six classes of disciples
- [Saitanaporn 2009] Phramonchai Saitanaporn, Buddhist Deliverance: A Re-evaluation of the Relationship Between Samatha and Vipassana (2009) — Discussion of the cultivation of samatha and vipassanā for abhiññā and vijjā in MN 73, and Buddhaghosa's commentary
- [Shonin et al. 2015] Edo Shonin, William Van Gordon, and Nirbhay N. Singh, eds., Buddhist Foundations of Mindfulness (2015) — Citation of MN 73 regarding developing serenity and insight together
- [Shi Huifeng and Orsborn 2012] Shi Huifeng and M. B. Orsborn, Chiasmus in Early Prajñāpāramitā (2012) — Comparison of MN 73 with parallel Chinese versions in SĀ and AltSĀ 198
- [Radich 2007] Michael David Radich, Somatics of Liberation (2007) — Attribution of non-returner status to lay followers and arahantship to monastics in MN 73
- [Wen, Study of Sukkhavipassaka] Tzungkuen Wen, A Study of Sukkhavipassaka in Pali Buddhism — Attainments of monastic disciples (arahants), celibate lay disciples (non-returners), and householders (once-returners)
- [Collett 2014] Alice Collett, ed., Women in Early Indian Buddhism (2014) — Reference to the PTS pagination (MN i 491) and the Buddha's count of over 500 arahant nuns and non-returner laywomen
